items.name: Generic Reference Counting (kref)
items.cortex_advantage: JavaScript GC handles object lifetime; manual refcounting adds get/put call pairs and risk of double-free
items.steel_man: kref_get_unless_zero() prevents use-after-free in concurrent delete+lookup races that GC does not prevent at the reference level

items.name: Maple Tree B-Tree for Range Storage
items.cortex_advantage: Cortex Map sufficient at <5000 entities; maple tree only pays off at >10k with range queries
items.steel_man: RCU-safe concurrent iteration eliminates flaw #46 at the data-structure level without application-level locking

items.name: Field-Level Locking Documentation Pattern
items.symbol: /* I: ... L: ... K: ... S: ... WQ: ... WR: ... */ comment convention
items.counter_case: Documentation rot — if a lock is refactored, mismatched comments are worse than no comments

items.name: LRU Walk Callback with 6-State Return Enum
items.symbol: enum lru_status { LRU_REMOVED, LRU_REMOVED_RETRY, LRU_ROTATE, LRU_SKIP, LRU_RETRY, LRU_STOP }
items.counter_case: Over-engineering for cache <5000 items; simple evict-oldest covers 95% of cases

items.name: seq_file Iterator Protocol for Large Tool Output
items.counter_case: MCP has its own streaming protocol; seq_file wrapper may conflict with MCP framing

items.name: Seqcount Optimistic Read-Retry for Snapshot-Safe Reads
items.counter_case: Node.js single-threaded; synchronous reads cannot be interrupted — only relevant if reads span await points

items.name: Workqueue Delayed + RCU-Deferred Work Variants
items.counter_case: JS already has setTimeout and Promise-based coordination; workqueue's shared pool doesn't apply to single-process Node.js

items.name: vruntime Deadline Comparison for Relevance Aging
items.counter_case: Adding time dimension to rankings increases tunability burden; high-scoring entities may unexpectedly drop on recency

items.name: Per-CPU Cache Counters
items.violated_principle: Local-first: JavaScript is single-threaded; per-CPU partitioning has no equivalent in V8

items.name: NUMA-Aware LRU Partitioning
items.violated_principle: Local-first: Cortex runs on a single dev machine; NUMA topology is irrelevant

items.name: Raw Spinlock with IRQ Disable
items.violated_principle: MCP-first: JavaScript event loop has no IRQ preemption; spinlocks busy-poll and block the event loop

items.name: Full RCU Implementation
items.violated_principle: Local-first: RCU requires OS scheduler tracking quiescent states per CPU; Node.js single event loop has no equivalent

items.name: Logarithmic CPU-Count Tunable Scaling
items.violated_principle: Local-first: Cortex is single-process; scaling by CPU count is irrelevant

items.name: vfs_cache_pressure as User-Configurable Tunable
items.counter_case: Default 10MB + 180 days covers nearly all users; tunable creates support burden without clear majority use case

items.name: Rollback-Safe Two-Phase Notifier Chain
items.counter_case: True fix for flaw #46 is eliminating shared state; rollback only cleans up after the race rather than preventing it

items.name: Shrinker count_objects/scan_objects Split
items.counter_case: Cortex has no memory pressure signals; count_objects would always return the same value without an external trigger

items.name: Negative Cache Tracking with Policy Flag
items.counter_case: Negative cache entries must be invalidated on file creation; stale 'not found' results returned until cache expiry

items.name: NORCU Flag — Skip-the-Safety Fast Path
items.pattern: Flag that bypasses deferred-reclaim safety for 'freshly allocated, never published' objects; correctness proof must survive all future refactors
items.proposed_action: Add CLAUDE.md rule: never add SKIP_CACHE_CHECK or NO_VALIDATION flags bypassing safety logic for freshly-created data
items.why_target_chose_it: Performance optimization for the extremely common case of short-lived dentries that never enter the RCU domain

items.name: Magic Numeric Constants Without Tunable Equivalent
items.pattern: Hardcoded 'good default' numeric constant with no user-facing escape hatch (Cortex: COMPACTION_THRESHOLD_BYTES = 10*1024*1024 with no cortex.json option)
items.proposed_action: Every numeric threshold in Cortex must have a corresponding cortex.json option; hardcoded value becomes the default
items.why_target_chose_it: Linux DOES expose this via sysctl; the anti-pattern is Cortex having constants with no sysctl-equivalent

items.name: Should cortex_find Use vruntime-Like Relevance Decay?
items.question: Should Cortex entities accumulate a 'virtual access time' that causes entities not searched recently to bubble up in cortex_find results?
alternatives: Bayesian aging penalty: tanh((now - lastAccessedAt) / HALF_LIFE_DAYS) * -0.2 score penalty
vruntime-style: each search hit adds to entity vruntime; lower vruntime = higher priority; prevents popular entities monopolizing results
No decay — search relevance should be content-based; recency is a separate --recent filter

items.name: At What Entity Count Does Augmented RB-Tree Beat Flat Map?
items.question: cortex_find does linear scan + sort; CFS uses augmented RB-tree for O(log n) min-priority retrieval. At what entity count does switching pay off?
alternatives: Profile at 100/1000/5000 entities; if Map+sort <5ms at 5000 entities, don't bother
Use MinHeap instead of full RB-tree for top-k results use case (simpler, same O complexity)
Adopt Maple Tree when entity count exceeds 10k — range queries and concurrent reads both benefit
